name: Abu al-Fath al-Busti
bio: Abu al-Fath Ali ibn Muhammad al-Busti, poet and state secretary, was born in Bust, near Sijistan, in what is now Afghanistan. As a young man he was secretary to the lord of Bust; when the emir Sebuktigin took the town he made al-Busti his trusted keeper of the chancery's secrets, and al-Busti went on to serve his son, Sultan Mahmud of Ghazna. He was famous for wordplay in verse and prose alike, which he called al-mutashabih, “the look-alike”; al-Tha'alibi called him “the master of the elegant manner in charming wordplay of original design”, and one of his prose sayings runs adat al-sadat sadat al-adat, “the habits of masters are the masters of habits”. His diwan is small, and his best-known poem is the Nuniyya. Mahmud later sent him away to Transoxiana, and he died a stranger at Uzjand, near Bukhara, in 400 AH (1010 CE), or by another account in 401.
